question_text: An algorithm examines all n! order ings. Describe why buying a processor twice as fast does not remove its scalability problem as n grows, and state one memory-saving implementation choice.
adaptation_rationale: Retains factorial-workload/hardware trade off reasoning under explicit scalability/time-space scope; does not classify the problem as NP merely because enumeration is expensive.
solution: The number of order ings grows factorially.; A factor-of-two speed up reduces a fixed run’s time but does not change that growth class.; Increasing n can therefore overwhelm the hardware improvement.; Generate/process one ordering at a time instead of storing all permutations simultaneously.
